newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dutch prince visits Mandela's former prison.
newsitem.headline: Dutch prince visits Mandela's former prison.

text.p: Dutch Prince Willem Alexander on Thursday toured the island fortress built by Dutch settlers in the 17th century where South Africa's prisoner turned president Nelson Mandela was jailed for 18 years.

During an informal press briefing on Robben Island, Willem said Mandela's commitment to forgiveness and reconciliation was praiseworthy, and he hoped that the closing of the prison would further spur on reconciliation.

The prison island has over the centuries been tranformed from a prison to a lunatic asylum, a leper colony and then a prison again. Mandela, now 78, spent 18 years of his 27-year term of imprisonment there for fighting apartheid.

Last month, the South African cabinet decided the sandstone prison should become a Museum of the Freedom Struggle. The 50 prison staff families and 110 non-political inmates still jailed there have to leave the island by January 1, 1997.
The Dutch crown prince was accompanied by Mandela's long-time friend and political adviser Ahmed Kathrada.
He visited Mandela's former cell and the lime quarry that doctors say have damaged the president's eyes.
In the 1980s, the Netherlands was in the forefront of the drive for sanctions to be imposed on South Africa for its racist policies.
An anti-racist guerrilla group torched a string of Royal Dutch Shell outlets in protest against its investments in South Africa.
Kathrada said the visit was important because of the historic ties that existed between the two countries.
"In our own little way, this is to say thank you to you and the people of your country for the support you showed during our struggle," Kathrada told the crown prince.
At the end of the visit, Willem wrote a few words in the prison visitor's book, saying: "I am very impressed with your historic site. A few minutes can't tell a story but it gave a good impression."
He was on the island for about two hours and had a light lunch in the prison dining hall.
Willem is accompanying his mother, Queen Beatrix, on a four-day state visit to South Africa.
